I love this about music and art in general. You don't need to pick it apart or find reasons why it pleases you, though that can increase the enjoyment of the piece.

It's so interesting how certain notes or chords are "happy" and others are "sad" in western music scales. I can't help but wonder why music is so ingrained in humans. Our brains are much deeper and more complex than the part that is conscious.

I have an idea that each person is relatively alike and unalike, that each person will be able to generally recognize a concept while still bringing their own unique perspective to shine anew how a concept can be viewed. For music, there certainly is a theory, one that resonates with the human mind, and I believe this is what makes music good. However, it does not mean that the theory is defined to a strict concept. That is why music is able to transcend most restrictive concepts like launguage. Music ideally is irrational at some extent. Write a song that sounds cheerful and give it cheerful lyrics, and you will construct a cheerful message. But create a melancholic tune in contrast to its lyrics, you are left with a depth, a feeling or description that transcends even the words. And that I find interesting. That is why I love this song and really all of the music from this show, especially the works attributed to the band. They aren't hollow songs, devoid of meaning, and while that meaning can lie in their literal context, something about its presentation allows it to be understood without being comprehended.

But that does not mean that that one thought is the right thought, it is more of a sensation of the individual, that personal look into what you think, what you feel that is important. Certainly, we can argue that a song is a certain way to display a specific idea, but to say that any other idea is then wrong is absurd. The song, just like the words of any human is interpreted through the lens of our own understanding. And that is why I like music, and honestly wish I was more musically inclined. It is probably one of the most honest works a person can make. And when done purely, speaks straight from the soul.
